question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cosecant function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsch}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡x+\operatorname{arcsch}⁡({x}^{2}+1)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡x)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsch}⁡({x}^{2}+1)) \\  & =\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}+(-\frac{1}{|{x}^{2}+1|\sqrt{1+({x}^{2}+1)^{2}}})\cdot ({x}^{2}+1)^{′} \\  & =\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}-\frac{1}{({x}^{2}+1)\sqrt{1+{x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+1}}\cdot 2x \\  & =\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}(1-\frac{2x}{\sqrt{{x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+2}}).\end{aligned}
$$
